idiom_name: index.ts API facade with explicit re-exports (`export ... from`); class facade with access modifiers
implementation_notes: In TypeScript the public API is the module graph: an index.ts that re-exports a curated set (export { CheckoutFacade } from './checkout/CheckoutFacade.js'; export type { Cart } from './checkout/types.js') is the facade, while export * barrels accidentally promote every internal to API. Use a class with private/readonly members for a stateful facade, keep subsystem modules unreachable from the entry point, and use export type so types travel the same boundary as values. The structure is ordinary TypeScript; the discipline is naming each export deliberately.
pitfalls: `export *` turns every internal into public API and complicates refactoring and tree-shaking; name exports explicitly.
Type-only re-exports must use `export type` (or type-only import forms) or isolatedModules-style builds emit dangling imports.
Structural typing means an exported interface is matched by shape: adding a field is a breaking change for implementers elsewhere, so keep facade types closed and versioned.
Path aliases and deep imports let consumers bypass the entry module; enforce the boundary with package exports (or lint rules) if it matters.
